scope: Public scholarly abstracts and one FDA PMA record; curated examples for stage/claim boundaries, not model quality or clinical-accuracy evaluation.

cases.sourceTitle: Deep Learning for Ear-EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interface: A Systematic Comparison and Design Insights.
cases.sourceText: In this study, we retrospectively analyze the ear-EEG dataset of a previous study in which a real-time endogenous BCI was evaluated using conventional machine learning. Specifically, we present an offline benchmark of 23 deep neural network architectures originally developed for scalp-EEG, which were adapted to ear-EEG and evaluated under an identical validation framework. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic comparison of this breadth for ear-EEG-based mental-task classification. Beyond conventional performance comparison, we identify the optimal architecture by jointly considering statistical significance and a performance-cost trade-off, incorporating classification accuracy, parameter count, and measured computational cost. Our results demonstrate that FBLightConvNet achieves the highest classification accuracy among all evaluated models and outperforms common spatial pattern-linear discriminant analysis (CSP-LDA), a widely adopted and robust conventional baseline, on all three recording days, with the difference reaching statistical significance on Days 2 and 3.
cases.evidence: Specifically, we present an offline benchmark of 23 deep neural network architectures originally developed for scalp-EEG, which were adapted to ear-EEG and evaluated under an identical validation framework.
conditions: we retrospectively analyze the ear-EEG dataset of a previous study in which a real-time endogenous BCI was evaluated using conventional machine learning.
on all three recording days, with the difference reaching statistical significance on Days 2 and 3.
cases.validSummary: 该研究对既有 ear-EEG 数据集离线比较了 23 种网络架构；结果限于相同验证框架和三个记录日，不代表在线患者控制。
cases.incorrectClaim: 这项研究证明系统能在线读心并改善患者功能。

cases.factTitle: 猕猴皮层内 BCI 导航实验
cases.sourceTitle: Intracortical brain-computer interface for navigation in virtual reality in macaque monkeys.
cases.sourceText: We present an innovative intracortical brain-computer interface (BCI) to bridge the gap between laboratory settings and real-world applications. This BCI approach introduces three key advancements. First, we used neural signals from three macaque brain regions-primary motor, dorsal, and ventral premotor cortex-enabling precise and flexible decoding of real-time three-dimensional (3D) sphere/avatar velocities. Second, we developed a realistic, immersive 3D virtual reality setup with dynamic camera tracking, allowing continuous navigation and obstacle avoidance that closely mimic real-world scenarios. Last, our BCI approach is very well suited for use by paralyzed patients, featuring a brief passive fixation without overt movements and closed-loop operation without retraining of the decoder during online decoding, relying on the user's neural plasticity and the decoder's robust generalization across tasks.
cases.evidence: we used neural signals from three macaque brain regions-primary motor, dorsal, and ventral premotor cortex-enabling precise and flexible decoding of real-time three-dimensional (3D) sphere/avatar velocities.
conditions: First, we used neural signals from three macaque brain regions-primary motor, dorsal, and ventral premotor cortex
Second, we developed a realistic, immersive 3D virtual reality setup with dynamic camera tracking

cases.factTitle: 48 名健康受试者 P300 实验
cases.sourceTitle: A Few-Channel Brain-Computer Interface System Based on a Heuristic Algorithm.
cases.sourceText: To enhance practicality, this paper proposes a fixed few-channel selection framework based on a heuristic algorithm to balance decoding performance and user experience. We integrated a genetic algorithm (GA) with Bayesian linear discriminant analysis (BLDA) to identify a strongly generalizable few-channel combination from a traditional eight-channel system, avoiding costly subject-specific recalibration. Validating this method, 48 healthy subjects completed rigorous offline and online virtual reality (VR) experiments. Results showed that the proposed three-channel system maintained highly comparable accuracy and information transfer rates to the eight-channel system, showing no significant performance degradation. Crucially, the few-channel scheme reduced equipment preparation time by 90% (from 30 to 3 min). Furthermore, NASA-TLX workload evaluations confirmed a significant reduction in users' psychological and physical burdens (p < 0.05).
cases.evidence: 48 healthy subjects completed rigorous offline and online virtual reality (VR) experiments.
conditions: 48 healthy subjects completed rigorous offline and online virtual reality (VR) experiments.

cases.incorrectClaim: 该系统已在患者中验证疗效并获准治疗。

cases.factTitle: 两名四肢瘫痪患者打字结果
cases.sourceTitle: Restoring rapid natural bimanual typing with a neuroprosthesis after paralysis.
cases.sourceText: This typing neuroprosthesis performed well for two iBCI clinical trial participants with tetraplegia-one with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and one with spinal cord injury. Typing speed is user-regulated, reaching 110 characters per minute, resulting in 22 words per minute with a word error rate of 1.6%. This resembles able-bodied typing accuracy and provides higher throughput than current state-of-the-art hand motor iBCI decoding. In summary, a typing neuroprosthesis decoding finger movements, provides an intuitive, familiar and easy-to-learn paradigm for individuals with impaired communication due to paralysis.
cases.evidence: This typing neuroprosthesis performed well for two iBCI clinical trial participants with tetraplegia-one with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and one with spinal cord injury.
conditions: two iBCI clinical trial participants with tetraplegia-one with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and one with spinal cord injury.

cases.incorrectClaim: 该研究已证明脑机接口对所有瘫痪患者有效。

cases.sourceTitle: Intermittent theta burst stimulation enhances the efficacy of brain-computer interface in upper limb rehabilitation post-stroke.
cases.sourceText: This exploratory single-center randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 18 subacute stroke patients, randomized to: BCI group (conventional rehab + BCI training) or iTBS + BCI group (conventional rehab + iTBS applied to the affected M1 cortex followed sequentially by BCI training). Interventions occurred 10 times over 2 weeks. Primary outcome: Fugl-Meyer Assessment - Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) score. Secondary outcomes: Modified Barthel Index (MBI), BCI task accuracy (BCI-TA). Mechanistic measures: sensorimotor cortex ERD and Laterality Index (LI). In this exploratory study, FMA-UE improvement was greater in the iTBS + BCI group, with significant differences at week 4 (Z = 2.569, p = 0.008). iTBS + BCI group showed a greater BCI-TA increase (87.22 ± 10.83% vs. 68.24 ± 5.75%, p = 0.041). This exploratory study suggests that sequential iTBS combined with BCI may have potential benefits in enhancing upper limb function in stroke patients.
cases.evidence: This exploratory single-center randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 18 subacute stroke patients
conditions: FMA-UE improvement was greater in the iTBS + BCI group, with significant differences at week 4 (Z = 2.569, p = 0.008).
cases.validSummary: 这项单中心探索性随机试验纳入 18 名亚急性卒中患者并报告了 4 周结果；结论限于该试验设计和终点。
cases.incorrectClaim: 该试验证明联合治疗已对卒中患者普遍有效。

cases.factTitle: 无线 BCI 原型验证
cases.sourceTitle: Secure wireless communication of brain-computer interface and mind control of smart devices enabled by space-time-coding metasurface.
cases.sourceText: We propose a deep fusion coding scheme that combines the BCI visual stimulation coding with metasurface space-time coding at the physical layer, enabling reliable and secure information transfers between the human brain and external devices. A brain space-time-coding metasurface platform is designed to implement a secure wireless communication system by using harmonic-encrypted beams. We design and fabricate a proof-of-principle prototype and experimentally show that the proposed wireless BCI scheme can establish a remote but safeguarded paradigm for human-machine interactions and intelligent metasurfaces, providing a potential direction in future secure wireless communications.
cases.evidence: We design and fabricate a proof-of-principle prototype and experimentally show that the proposed wireless BCI scheme can establish a remote but safeguarded paradigm for human-machine interactions
conditions: A brain space-time-coding metasurface platform is designed to implement a secure wireless communication system by using harmonic-encrypted beams.
cases.validSummary: 研究制造并测试了无线 BCI 原理验证原型；原文没有据此证明患者实验、注册批准、商业供货或真实部署。
cases.incorrectClaim: 这套原型已在患者日常环境中部署并获批销售。

regulatoryApproval.sourceTitle: FDA Premarket Approval P100026 - NeuroPace RNS System
regulatoryApproval.sourceText: Device: NEUROPACE RNS SYSTEM. Generic Name: Implanted brain stimulator for epilepsy. Applicant: NeuroPace, Inc. PMA Number: P100026. Decision Date: 11/14/2013. APPROVAL FOR THE RNS SYSTEM. THIS DEVICE IS INDICATED AS FOLLOWS: AS AN ADJUNCTIVE THERAPY IN REDUCING THE FREQUENCY OF SEIZURES IN INDIVIDUALS 18 YEARS OF AGE OR OLDER WITH PARTIAL ONSET SEIZURES WHO HAVE UNDERGONE DIAGNOSTIC TESTING THAT LOCALIZEDNO MORE THAN 2 EPILEPTOGENIC FOCI, ARE REFRACTORY TO TWO OR MORE ANTIEPILEPTIC MEDICATIONS, AND CURRENTLY HAVE FREQUENT AND DISABLING SEIZURES. THE RNS SYSTEM HAS DEMONSTRATED SAFETY AND EFFECTIVENESS IN PATIENTS WHO AVERAGE 3 OR MORE DISABLING SEIZURES PER MONTH OVER THE THREE MOST RECENT MONTHS, AND HAS NOT BEEN EVALUATED IN PATIENTS WITH LESS FREQUENT SEIZURES.

regulatoryApproval.validSummary: FDA 的 PMA 记录显示 RNS System 于 2013 年获批，用作满足年龄、诊断、用药和发作频率条件的成人部分性癫痫辅助治疗；不适用于记录未评估的人群。
regulatoryApproval.incorrectClaim: FDA 已批准 RNS System 用于所有癫痫患者和所有适应证。
